OSPWithout CodecOverview

System Overview

System Overview

A dsPIC33AK512MPS512 samples line-in audio with its own ADC, outputs audio as 192 kHz PWM, synthesises AVAS engine sound and drives an OSP LED strip, all controlled over LIN from a SAMA5D27 touch-screen HMI. No external audio codec is used.

RF11 must be an input before osp_init()

MCC sets TRISF = 0x07EF (RF11 output, left over from the codec SPI1 SDO). Driven low, RF11 pulls SIOP low through U3, the supply test on RF8 reads 0 V and the strip never answers. OSP_Board_Init() sets TRISFbits.TRISF11 = 1, as in osp/firmware (TRISF = 0x0BEF).

3.3Interrupt priorities

Table 3-2: Priorities as set in code

SourcePriorityRateWork
PWM3 (_PWM3Interrupt)5192 kHzNoise shaping, write PG5DC / PG3DC

DMA0–DMA31per OSP frameSPI2 TX / SPI4 RX

OSP frame start is atomic

osp.c disables interrupts for about 2 µs around the DMA software trigger and DISSDO = 0. If the PWM3 or ADC ISR hits in that gap, the first Manchester bytes leave with SDO disabled and the LEDs drop the frame (CRC error).

3.4Main loop

Figure 3-2: Initialisation and main loop flowchart

▭ Rounded = start▭ Rectangle = process◇ Diamond = decisionReturn path joins the No branch
Why Modbus is not polled

nmbs_server_poll() blocks up to 10 ms waiting for a byte. That made the 1 ms tasks run every ~10 ms (slow blip, late LIN response), so the AVAS loop calls only RefEngine_Fill(), LIN_Slave_Process() and OSP_UpdateEffects(). RefEngine_Fill() is called three times per pass to keep the FIFO full.

PWM update order

AudioISR_Process() calls SetPWMDuty() with the previous sample first, then AudioTasks(). This keeps the time between UPDREQ and the PWM SOC window short; the cost is one sample of latency.

Audio-Reactive LEDs

How the LINE IN signal becomes a VU meter on the OSP strip: 32-sample blocks, two one-pole low-pass filters that split bass, mids and treble, RMS energy with attack/decay smoothing, a palette per dominant band, CENTER / EDGE mapping and a white beat flash.

5.1Processing pipeline

Figure 5-1: From audio sample to LED (interrupt part shaded)

AudioTasks()48 kHz, phone mode output L/R
32 samples
osp_block[64]interleaved L,R; zeros in engine mode
1500 /s
OSP_Audio_Process()analyze_audio(), every 8th block sets update_pending
187.5 /s
OSP_Audio_UpdateLEDs()main loop, every pass
render
render_vu_meter()osp_SETPWM per LED → SPI2 DMA
No SPI inside the interrupt

OSP_Audio_Process() runs inside _AD4CH7Interrupt and only does the analysis. It sets update_pending; all osp_SETPWM() calls happen in the main loop. The analyser runs only while initialized and led_enabled are true.

5.4Band split with two low-pass filters

Table 5-4: init_filters() and analyze_audio()

ItemFormula / value
Monox = (L + R) × 0.5
Filtery[n] = α·x[n] + (1 − α)·y[n−1]
lpf_500α = 0.044196 → fc = −fs/2π · ln(1 − α) = 345 Hz
lpf_2000α = 0.208247 → fc = 1784 Hz
Basslp1 = lpf_500(x)
Midslp2 − lp1
Treblex − lp2
Statey_prev kept across blocks (continuous filter)
Names versus real cut-off

The filters are called lpf_500 and lpf_2000, and the comments say “500 Hz” and “2000 Hz for 48 kHz”. The alpha values give 345 Hz and 1784 Hz. FREQ_LOW_CUTOFF (300) and FREQ_MID_CUTOFF (2000) in the header are not used. The three bands always add up to the input (bass + mids + treble = x), so no energy is lost; the bands are wide and overlap (one-pole slopes, 6 dB/octave).

Figure 5-2: Band-split block diagram (analyze_audio())

Navy boxes = state kept between blocksΣ = adder with the signs shownLeft of the dashed line: every sample; right: once per 32-sample blockBass + mids + treble = x

Figure 5-3: One-pole low-pass filter (lowpass()): y[n] = α·x[n] + (1 − α)·y[n−1]

Table 5-4a: Filter coefficients and gains (computed from α at fs = 48 kHz)

Filterα1 − αfc100 Hz1 kHz5 kHz
lpf_5000.0441960.955804345 Hz−0.3 dB−9.7 dB−23.1 dB
lpf_20000.2082470.7917531784 Hz0.0 dB−1.2 dB−9.3 dB
How it works

Each sample, the output moves a fraction α of the way towards the input. Small α = slow change = lower cut-off. fc = −fs / 2π · ln(1 − α). Slope 6 dB per octave above fc. One multiply-add per sample; y_prev is static, so the filter runs on across blocks.

Figure 5-4: Magnitude response of the three bands, computed from the alpha values at fs = 48 kHz

Reading the table

Amplitude is at the analyser, after the ×3.5 phone gain, so 0.10 there is about 0.029 at the ADC. The bass gain of 15 makes a 100 Hz tone fill the strip already at 0.10. A 1 kHz tone leaks into all three bands because the one-pole filters are wide.

AVAS Engine Sound

The control layer turns LIN commands into a target RPM and a fade gain; the reference engine synth renders 32-sample blocks in the main loop into a FIFO that the audio ISR reads one sample at a time.

Table 6-1: avas_ctrl.h with USE_REF_ENGINE = 1

DefineValueMeaning
AVAS_RPM_IDLE900Lowest RPM, fallback

AVAS_THROTTLE_RPM_LIFT0No extra RPM from throttle
AVAS_THROTTLE_DEFAULT100Until LIN 0x12 arrives
AVAS_FADE_MS50Gain step 1 / (48 × 50) per sample

6.2Reference engine

Table 6-2: ref_engine.c / ref_engine.h

ItemValue
InitEngineSynthWrap_init(&s, 48000, ENG_V8, 0, 1, 0.2, 2)
Start valuesRPM 0, throttle 0.3, noise_mix = 0.055
RPM slewcore.rpm_slew_per_s (default 3000 RPM/s)
Block32 samples (REF_ENGINE_BLOCK), left channel used
FIFO32 blocks = 1024 floats = 4 KB = 21.3 ms
Output gainREF_ENGINE_OUT_GAIN = 1.0
UnderrunReturns 0.0, counter printed as [ENGINE] FIFO underruns
Why a FIFO

One engine_process() block takes longer than one 20.8 µs sample interrupt. The main loop is the only producer and the ISR the only consumer, so fifo_wr / fifo_rd need no lock. 21 ms covers the longest stall seen: printf at 115 200 baud costs ~87 µs per character.

6.4Blip envelope

Figure 6-2: RPM after LIN 0x13 from 1500 RPM, computed from blip_update()

Blip rules

Ignored while AVAS is off. A new blip restarts from the current RPM, so re-triggering mid-blip is smooth. The decay returns to the live target, so RPM changes during decay are followed. AVAS_IsBlipRising() (attack + hold) drives the white flash of the tachometer when it is enabled.

OSP LED Control

Colour scaling

LIN Protocol

Receive-only LIN slave on UART2: one frame ID with four data bytes, signal ID in D0 and values in D1 to D3, classic checksum.

8.1Frame layout

Figure 8-1: Frame LIN_ID_SG_GCM_02 (ID 0x22, PID 0xE2)

BREAK≥13 bit, FERIF
0x55SYNC
0xE2PID (ID 0x22)
D0Signal ID
D1value / R / RPM_H
D2value / G / RPM_L
D3value / B
CHKclassic, data only
UART2 settingValue
BaudU2BRG = 100 MHz / 115200 = 868 → 115 207
RegistersU2CON = 0x8000000, U2STAT = 0x2E0080 (RXWM = 0)
RXISR priority 2, 64-entry ring buffer, bit 8 = framing error
Data lengthID 0x00–0x1F: 2, 0x20–0x2F: 4, 0x30–0x3F: 8
Parser stateNext on
LIN_STATE_IDLE0x00 → BREAK; 0x55 → SYNC
LIN_STATE_BREAK0x55 → SYNC; other non-zero → IDLE
LIN_STATE_SYNCPID parity OK → DATA, else error → IDLE
LIN_STATE_DATAafter data_len bytes → CHECKSUM
LIN_STATE_CHECKSUMmatch → callback; always → IDLE
Break handling

A byte 0x00 with the framing error flag always restarts a frame, even in the middle of one. Every valid frame calls AVAS_LinAlive(); frames with another ID are logged and ignored.

8.2Signal table

Table 8-1: LIN_FrameHandler() in audio_demo.c

D0SignalPayloadFirmware action
0x01LED powerD3: 0 = ON, 1 = OFFON: OSP_SwitchToLedDemo(); OFF: audio LED off, strip cleared
0x02PatternD3: 0 = CENTER, 1 = EDGELED demo, SYNCHRONIZED mode
0x03Number of LEDsD3 (firmware adds 1)OSP_Audio_SetNumLEDs(D3 + 1), clamped to detected
0x05SourceD3: 0 = LINE, 1 = MICSYNCHRONIZED; both use ADC LINE IN
0x08LED style effectD3: 0–3STATIC mode + effect (Table 7-2)
0x09RGB colourD1 = R, D2 = G, D3 = BOSP_Audio_SetRGBColor()
0x0ABrightnessD3: 0–100 %× 255 / 100
0x10AVAS enableD3: 1 = ONFade in, ENGINE mode, audio LED off
0x11RPMD1 = high, D2 = lowClamped 900–5500, pot ignored afterwards
0x12ThrottleD3: 0–100 %RefEngine_SetThrottle(D3 / 100)
0x13BlipD3 = 1Envelope (Figure 6-2), only when AVAS on
0x14Engine typeD3: 0 = V8, 1 = BulletSets engine_type; no effect with USE_REF_ENGINE = 1
0x15Audio sourceD3: 0 = Engine, 1 = LINE INSets audio_mode
0x20 / 0x21 / 0x22Left / Right / ParkingD3: 0 / 1Mutually exclusive; unchanged repeats ignored

The SAMA5D27 WLSOM1-EK runs audio_led_gui_v6.py, a Python 3 standard-library GUI on an 800×480 touch display. It sends 8-byte LIN-style frames on /dev/ttyS2 to the MCP2003B master transceiver.

The project CLAUDE.md names a SAMA7D65 with PyQt5. The HMI sources and their CLAUDE.md describe a SAMA5D27 WLSOM1-EK with a standard-library GUI. This guide follows the HMI sources.

State resets

Entering AVAS resets the Style and Factory screen state. Going back from Style or Factory to the menu resets the AVAS screen state (indicators off, RPM 0), but sends no frames. Only the engine on/off state is kept.

How to get the VU meter from the HMI

Open Audio LED Controller → Factory Settings and press Line In (or a pattern). Style → APPLY switches the strip to the static effects; Factory source or pattern switches it back to the VU meter.

9.5Frame format

Figure 9-16: AudioLEDController.send_frame()

0x00break
0x55sync
0xE2PID
CMDD0
B3D1
B4D2
B5D3
CHKclassic
Break byte

The HMI sends the break as a normal 0x00 UART byte (9 low bits), not a 13-bit LIN break. The firmware parser accepts it through its fallback path: in LIN_STATE_IDLE a 0x00 byte without framing error also moves to LIN_STATE_BREAK.

9.8Build, test and deploy

# PC: render all graphics into gui_assets.bin (Pillow + Noto Sans)
python3 tools/build_assets.py
# PC: run the real screens with a fake framebuffer and UART, write screenshots/v6/*.png, print frames
python3 tools/simulate.py

# Deploy v6 to the board and point the service at it
scp audio_led_gui_v6.py gui_assets.bin audio_led_gui_v5.py root@<board-ip>:/root/
ssh root@<board-ip> "sed -i 's#/root/audio_led_gui_v5.py#/root/audio_led_gui_v6.py#' /etc/systemd/system/audioled.service && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart audioled"

# On the board
systemctl status audioled
journalctl -u audioled -f

# Send a frame from a PC USB-UART (Engine ON)
stty -F /dev/ttyUSB0 115200 raw -echo cs8 -cstopb -parenb
printf '\x00\x55\xE2\x10\x00\x00\x01\xEE' > /dev/ttyUSB0
Service still points at v5

The audioled.service file in the HMI folder runs /root/audio_led_gui_v5.py. Apply the sed above so the board starts v6.

Shared unionfx_shared_ram: Reverb_t (19.6 KB) and UnifiedDelay_t (19.3 KB) share one area in AVAS_MODE

Check the map file after every change

A stack overflow shows as an endless reset with RCON = 0x40 (SW reset from traps.c). The start-up banner prints the reset cause on UART1.

11.3Technical findings

Table 11-1: Code review findings

IDSeverityAreaFindingSuggested action
F1MediumIndicatorOSP_DrawIndicatorWave() splits at a fixed LED 21. With fewer than 22 LEDs, right_count = num_leds - 21 wraps (uint8_t), the left wave draws nothing, and the right wave writes LED addresses that do not exist.Use half = min(21, num_leds / 2) or skip the left half when num_leds ≤ 21.
F2MediumAVASWith USE_REF_ENGINE = 1 the engine is always ENG_V8; LIN 0x14 and SW2 only change an unused variable. The start-up text still prints “SW2: Toggle V8/Bullet” and “Single-cylinder thumper”.Pass the engine type to EngineSynthWrap_init(), or remove the option and the text.
F3LowAVASAVAS_LIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 0: if the HMI stops, the engine keeps the last RPM.Enable once the HMI sends frames periodically.
F4LowInterruptsComments in osp_board.c and adc_audio.h say AD4CH7 runs at priority 6; INTERRUPT_Initialize() sets 4 (6 only with FIR_DECIMATION). Behaviour is fine (PWM3 at 5 pre-empts).Correct the comments.
F5LowPinspins.c still maps SPI1 SDO1/SCK1/SDI1 to RF11/RF9/RF8, SS1 to RB12/RG2, REFO1 to RG0 and PCI8. osp_init() overwrites the RF pins; the rest is unused with NO_CODEC.Remove the codec routes in MCC.
F6LowCommentsadc_audio.h says the XPRO1 inputs are RB3/RB4; the code uses AD4AN0 = RB4 and AD4AN1 = RB6.Correct the comment.
F7ClosedPinsRB4 (left audio in, pin 57) is also PGC1. The DIM ICSP header (Figure 2-3) uses PGD3 / PGC3, so there is no conflict.None.
F8LowTestS1 + S2 at start-up sets loopback mode (400 Hz tone), but AudioTasks() returns before the tone code in AVAS_MODE.Remove the check from the AVAS build or move the tone into the AVAS path.
F9LowTimingLIN_DEBUG = 1 prints one line per frame on UART1 (~87 µs per character, blocking).Set 0 for production.
F10LowOSPOSP_Audio_SetNumLEDs() turns off LEDs from i = num_leds, which is the last active LED, not the first unused one.Start at num_leds + 1.
F11MediumVUCENTER pattern with an even LED count starts at ps + 1 / ps + 2 (LEDs 22 / 23 for 42), so the meter is off-centre by one and LED 1 is never written.Use left = ps − i, right = ps + 1 + i for even N.
F12MediumHMIHMI LED count is 10–254 (default 60); the firmware adds 1 and clamps to the detected count (max 42), so 60 always becomes “all LEDs” and the HMI status shows a value the strip does not use.Limit the HMI slider to 1–42, or report the detected count back.
F13MediumHMIThe HMI never sends 0x12 throttle, 0x13 blip, 0x14 engine type or 0x15 audio source. The AVAS “Throttle %” is RPM / 8000 and not sent.Add controls or drop the features from the firmware description.
F14LowVUBEAT_HOLD_FRAMES = 20 is counted per analysis block (1500 /s), so the hold is 13.3 ms, not the ~100 ms in the comment. The 0.92 history average has τ = 8 ms.Count in render frames, or raise the value to ~150.
F15LowVUFilter names and comments say 500 Hz / 2 kHz; the alphas give 345 Hz / 1784 Hz.Compute alpha from fc or rename.
F16LowHMIThe HMI sends the break as a 0x00 byte. It works only through the parser fallback, not as a real LIN break.Send a real break (tcsendbreak or baud switch) on the master side.
F17LowHMIOpening Audio LED Controller sends nothing, and Power shows ON without having sent it. The strip stays in its previous state until the first command.Send the current menu state when the screen opens.
F18LowHMIaudioled.service still starts v5.Point it at v6 (Section 9.8).
F19LowDocsProject CLAUDE.md names SAMA7D65 + PyQt5; HMI sources are SAMA5D27 + standard library.Update CLAUDE.md.
